findings.enhancement_type: worked mechanism expansion for Topic 1 storage layers and fsync semantics
findings.change: Add Worked storage layers and POSIX fsync() durability boundaries to Topic 1 technical discussion
findings.anchor_str: # Explicit worked boundaries supplement, rather than replace, existing depth.
findings.drafted_text:
DATA['topics'][0]['technical'] += '
Worked storage layers and POSIX fsync() durability boundaries
  • Concrete example: When a container process writes transaction records to /data/orders.log, the write() system call enters the kernel page cache and returns immediately. If the container crashes or the host loses power before dirty pages are flushed to non-volatile storage, uncommitted records vanish. Calling fsync() or fdatasync() forces the kernel to flush file pages and metadata to disk, establishing transactional durability.
  • OverlayFS stacks multiple read-only lowerdir layers beneath a single read-write upperdir layer. Modifying an existing file triggers a Copy-on-Write (COW) replication, copying the entire file from the lower layer to the upper layer before applying edits, which creates severe I/O penalties for large database files. In contrast, Docker named volumes and host bind mounts bypass OverlayFS entirely, directly mounting host directory paths and preserving standard POSIX filesystem semantics.
  • Evidence limit: Local filesystem benchmarks and fsync() latencies reflect local kernel cache flushing behavior; they do not simulate cloud storage network attachments, distributed replication, or multi-zone durability guarantees.
'
